question: What is the main focus of a community diagnosis compared to an individual diagnosis?

options.A: The specific medical history of the village chief
options.B: The financial records of a local clinic
options.C: A single patient inside a hospital ward
options.D: An entire population within a specific boundary

explanation: Community diagnosis evaluates the health status and needs of an entire group of people rather than focusing on a single patient. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is establishing baseline health data important during a community assessment?

options.A: It proves that the health workers have finished their assignment
options.B: It eliminates all infectious diseases in the local area instantly
options.C: It provides a starting point to measure future health changes
options.D: It guarantees immediate funding from international donor agencies

explanation: Baseline data serves as a reference point to track progress and evaluate the success of health interventions over time. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h1)

question: What type of community diagnosis involves a rapid observation of a neighborhood by walking or driving through?
explanation: A windshield or familiarization survey relies on direct observation to quickly gather visual data about a community's environment. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h2)

question: When is a comprehensive needs assessment most appropriate for a health team to use?

options.A: When the healthcare team only has two hours to visit the village
options.B: When the community has no water supply and needs immediate rescue
options.C: When the local government wants to avoid spending money on surveys
options.D: When detailed data on all health and social aspects is required

explanation: Comprehensive assessments take more resources but are necessary when an in-depth understanding of every health determinant is needed. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the first chronological phase to complete before gathering data in a community?
explanation: The pre-survey phase involves securing permissions, planning logistics, and mobilizing community leaders before any actual data collection begins. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h3)

question: What core elements must be clearly linked inside a proper community diagnostic statement?

options.A: The name of the nurse, the hospital budget, and the vehicle number
options.B: The health problem, its underlying cause, and the affected population
options.C: The political party in power and the weather condition of the village
options.D: The personal phone numbers of all traditional rulers in the state

explanation: A complete community diagnosis clearly specifies what the health problem is, why it is happening, and who is suffering from it. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h3)

question: Where does secondary data typically come from when conducting a community health assessment?

options.A: Focus group discussions held under the village tree
options.B: Existing hospital registers and census reports
options.C: Physical observations made during a windshield survey
options.D: Direct household interviews conducted by the nurse

explanation: Secondary data refers to information that has already been collected by others, such as previous census reports and hospital logbooks. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why should a nurse avoid relying only on clinic records for a community diagnosis?

options.A: Clinic registers are always completely blank and unusable
options.B: Government hospitals do not keep any medical records at all
options.C: Clinic records miss people who do not visit the health facility
options.D: Secondary data is illegal for public health nurses to read

explanation: Relying only on hospital records ignores individuals with health issues who never manage to visit a formal health facility. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h4)

question: What mathematical measures do nurses calculate to determine the frequency of diseases in a community?
explanation: Incidence and prevalence rates measure how frequently diseases occur or exist within a specified population over time. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why is comparing local community data with national health standards useful during analysis?

options.A: It reduces the cost of buying drugs for the clinic
options.B: It stops people from getting sick with malaria
options.C: It replaces the need to collect data from households
options.D: It helps identify how severe local health gaps are

explanation: Comparing local findings against broader standards highlights whether a local health issue is worse than the national average. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the primary reason for setting priorities after completing a community data analysis?

options.A: Resources are limited, so the most urgent problems must be addressed first
options.B: Minor health problems are completely unimportant to human survival
options.C: Community members refuse to discuss more than a single topic
options.D: Government policy forbids solving more than one health issue per year

explanation: Because money, time, and personnel are always limited, priority setting ensures the most critical health threats receive attention first. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h6)

question: A community has high rates of both common colds and severe cholera outbreaks. Which problem should the nursing team prioritize?

options.A: Whichever problem the youngest children vote for in a meeting
options.B: Common colds, because everyone in the village catches them easily
options.C: Cholera, because of its high severity and potential for rapid death
options.D: Neither, because both conditions clear up without any medical care

explanation: Seriousness and life-threatening nature are key criteria in priority setting, making a cholera outbreak much more urgent than common colds. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the main advantage of ensuring genuine community ownership in a health intervention?

options.A: It stops all natural disasters from happening in the region
options.B: It prevents the local government from ever auditing the clinic
options.C: It eliminates the need for nurses to visit the village ever again
options.D: It ensures the program continues long after external workers leave

explanation: Community ownership fosters sustainability, ensuring local residents maintain and protect the health program long-term. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h7)

question: Which group represents key stakeholders that a nurse must engage during community mobilization in Nigeria?

options.D: Foreign tourists visiting local wildlife parks

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders hold immense influence over local culture and decision-making, making their engagement crucial for success. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is the difference between monitoring and evaluation in a community health project?

options.A: Monitoring uses money, while evaluation is completely free of cost
options.B: Monitoring happens after the project closes, while evaluation happens before
options.C: Monitoring is ongoing tracking, while evaluation assesses final outcomes
options.D: Monitoring is done by villagers, while evaluation is done by foreigners

explanation: Monitoring occurs continuously during project implementation, whereas evaluation measures the final impact and success at the end. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h8)

question: Why are clear health indicators necessary when evaluating a community intervention?

options.A: They replace the need to talk with community leaders at meetings
options.B: They guarantee that the local clinic will receive a new ambulance
options.C: They prevent nurses from making mistakes during patient treatment
options.D: They provide measurable signs to show whether objectives were met

explanation: Indicators give concrete, measurable evidence regarding whether health goals and targets have been successfully accomplished. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h8)
